clue.text: Cunningly altering figure

indicators.note: done cunningly, the letters of the next word are craftily rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is slyly doctoring a number in the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a number being fiddled, but it is a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided polygon is a geometric figure, a shape drawn in plane geometry.

clue.text: Detected in-patient's heart beat faster than usual

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of the nine letters of in-patient

parts.note: the possessive word in-patient, nine letters once the hyphen and 's are set aside
a heart that raced beat unusually fast

explanation.surface: A hospital patient's heart was found to be pounding.
explanation.definitionFit: To have traced something is to have tracked it down, found or detected it.

clue.text: Annoyance among committee of adjudicators

parts.note: in means among, as in 'in the crowd'
a jury is a panel that judges, in court or in a contest

explanation.surface: Irritation spreads among the panel of judges.
explanation.walkthrough: Annoyance in its old sense of harm or hurt done to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Injury in an older sense is a wrong or harm done, a source of annoyance or grievance.

clue.text: Enjoy set articles regularly producing these features

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every second letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: Savouring a set of items brings about certain characteristics.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of 'Enjoy set articles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostrils are the openings of the nose, facial features one breathes through.

clue.text: Reportedly spill the beans one's bought from the greengrocer

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard, so the answer sounds like the synonym

parts.note: to leak a secret is to spill the beans

explanation.surface: A shopper gossips about the vegetables at the grocer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beans' and 'greengrocer' make it sound like produce; a greengrocer is a British fruit and vegetable shop.
explanation.definitionFit: This onion-family vegetable is an example of produce sold by a vegetable seller.

clue.text: Steps up tense atmosphere on board ship

indicators.note: something on board a ship sits inside it, so these letters go within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: Tension rises among the crew of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps leading to an upper floor is a staircase, the steps one climbs.

clue.text: Inheritors pursuing terrain primarily belonging to them

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the inheritors' word follows
primarily takes the leading letter of terrain

parts.note: heirs are those who inherit

explanation.surface: Heirs go after land that is chiefly their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Theirs is the possessive pronoun for something owned by those people.

clue.text: Treated with contempt, placed in isolation lacking means essentially

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word for placed in isolation

parts.note: insulated means isolated or cut off

indicators.note: essentially points to the core, the central letter of means

explanation.surface: Someone was scorned and shut away without the means to live.
explanation.walkthrough: INSULATED loses A, the middle letter of 'means'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be insulted is to be spoken to rudely, scorned or affronted.

clue.text: Basely confused about lines in segment of speech

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the lines
confused means the letters of basely are muddled into a new order

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Someone mumbles a muddled part of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllable is a unit of pronunciation, one beat of a spoken word.

clue.text: Regulated precisely following a draft initially by editor

indicators.note: following puts the synonym of precisely after the letters already in place
by means next to, so the editor's letters are placed alongside at the end
initially picks out the opening letter of the word draft

parts.note: just can mean exactly or precisely, as in 'just so'

explanation.surface: A document is tweaked exactly as its first version was edited.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusted machinery has been set or regulated to work correctly, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Ship retiring in hopeless event

indicators.note: retiring says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters are hidden within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boat drops out of a race it had no chance of winning.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it signals the hidden letters LESSEV across 'hopeless event'; 'retiring' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any boat or ship, the general seafaring term.

clue.text: Unit of measurement for each gold sovereign

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measurement
per means for each, as in 'per head'
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Valuing a gold coin by a set measure each.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' looks like the old gold coin, but it is a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme ruler of an empire, a sovereign monarch.

clue.text: Wrongdoings of naughty children not principally tolerated

indicators.note: not says the following letter is to be left out of the word for naughty children

parts.note: little terrors are badly behaved children

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of tolerated

explanation.surface: Misbehaving youngsters' misdeeds are not put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRORS loses T, the first letter of 'tolerated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors are mistakes, and wrongdoings in the sense of faults or lapses.

clue.text: It's not fair when this protection is required

definitions.text: It's not fair when this protection is required

parts.words: It's not fair when this protection is required
parts.note: 'not fair' sounds like a complaint of injustice, but means the weather is not fine: it is raining

explanation.surface: A grumble about injustice prompting a call for safeguards.
explanation.definitionFit: When the weather is not fair it rains, and a rain shield carried overhead keeps one dry.

clue.text: Obtain advantage from unusually fine bet

indicators.note: unusually says these letters appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A gambler profits from an oddly well-placed wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To benefit from something is to gain or profit by it.

clue.text: Made structural changes, given warning before shifting over a ton

indicators.note: shifting over says the letter for a ton is moved to another place in the word

parts.note: to be alerted is to have been given warning
T is the abbreviation for a ton

explanation.surface: A building is remodelled after a warning about a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the T of ALERTED one place along.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering something means modifying it, here changing a garment's or building's construction.

clue.text: Make acceptable little brother's room, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard, not seen, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a brother here is a monk, whose small room in a monastery is a cell

explanation.surface: Persuading parents that a younger sibling's bedroom is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little brother' suggests a younger sibling, but the brother is a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell an idea is to persuade others to accept it.

clue.text: Annoying thing is involved in subtle difference

indicators.note: involved in means placed within, so is goes inside the synonym for subtle difference

parts.note: a nuance is a fine distinction

explanation.surface: A tiny distinction causes irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is a person or thing causing bother or irritation.

clue.text: Announced day English nun died

parts.note: a Clare is a nun of the order of Poor Clares
D is the abbreviation for died, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A notice reports the date an English nun passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Clares are a Franciscan order of nuns, so one member is a Clare.
explanation.definitionFit: To have declared something is to have stated or proclaimed it publicly.

clue.text: Final word in a line

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: The last word written on a line of text.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminal means at the end, forming the last part, so final.

clue.text: Employs stratagems without reason at first

indicators.note: without means the letter that follows is dropped from the word for stratagems

parts.note: ruses are tricks or stratagems

indicators.note: at first selects the opening letter of reason

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to tricks without thinking things through.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something is to employ it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Withdraws troops on manoeuvres

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army troops
moves are manoeuvres, as in a game

explanation.surface: An army pulls back soldiers who are out on exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on manoeuvres' looks like an anagram signal but simply gives MOVES; the Royal Engineers are a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing something means taking it away, so withdrawing it.

clue.text: Registers resorts in Texas (not Cuba)

indicators.note: not says the following letter is to be left out of the American word

parts.note: centers is the American spelling of centres, holiday resorts
C is the internationally used vehicle registration letter for Cuba

explanation.surface: A tourist signs in at Texan resorts rather than Cuban ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Texas' asks for American spelling, CENTERS, and the Cuban C comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to record or register them.

clue.text: Blotted from memory second-class old city that is ultimately dead

parts.note: B is second class, after A
Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city
ie is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of dead

explanation.surface: A minor ancient city is now dead and forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A buried memory is one suppressed or deliberately forgotten, hidden away.

clue.text: Be present at a motorcycle race finish

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
end means finish

explanation.surface: A spectator turns up at the end of a motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to go to it and be there.

clue.text: Expend about pound on one daughter — very good

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pound sign goes inside the word for expend

parts.note: to expend is to spend
L is the symbol for a pound, from Latin libra
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Splashing out cash on a daughter is a fine thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid is an informal exclamation of approval, meaning excellent.

clue.text: Value of American horse

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: What a US racehorse is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a sum or quantity, the total value of something.

clue.text: Check weather broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast suggests something spoken on air, so a word that sounds alike

parts.note: rain is a kind of weather

explanation.surface: Look at the forecast on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like an instruction to look; it means restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain, hold back or check, as with a horse's reins.

clue.text: Tended sick shark beached finally

parts.note: a nurse shark is a type of shark

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of beached

explanation.surface: Someone looked after an ailing shark stranded on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' sits in the surface as colour but is not used: the shark is a NURSE shark.
explanation.definitionFit: To have nursed someone is to have cared for or tended them.

clue.text: Period intervening in poor sentence

parts.note: mean can mean poor or shabby
time is a prison sentence, as in 'doing time'

explanation.surface: An interval spent serving a harsh jail term.
explanation.definitionFit: The meantime is the interval between two events, a period in between.

clue.text: Some high-level destiny for first-born

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lofty fate awaits the first child in a family.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest child is the oldest, the one born before the siblings.

clue.text: Surprisingly lucid end made part of set

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at letters ending up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A clear ending unexpectedly found its way into a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something included has been taken in as a member of a group.
